text:
Simple time-of-flight measurement of the speed of
sound using smartphones
S. Staacks, S. Hütz, H. Heinke, C. Stampfer
Institute of Physics I and II, RWTH Aachen University
We propose an easy experiment that allows to determine the speed of sound through a simple time-
of-flight measurement using two smartphones. The concept of using the sensors in mobile phones
for physics experiments has become a well-known option for science teachers12345. Since these
devices are readily available to most students and teachers, experiments can be set up at little to no
costs while generating fascination and motivation for the students thanks to the novelty of using
their own devices in an unusual way. From all the sensors available in modern phones, the
microphone
title: Staacks 2018 Simple Time of Flight Speed of Sound Smartphones

text:
e novelty of using
their own devices in an unusual way. From all the sensors available in modern phones, the
microphone offers the best temporal resolution by a huge margin as it records samples at a rate of
(typically) 48 kHz. As this fast sampling rate is a requirement for high quality audio recordings it
has been around long before smartphones offered other sensors, and audio inputs have already been
used for experiments on soundcards in desktop computers678.
Consequently, the microphone is at the center of a variety of phone-based experiments to determine
the speed of sound. The experimental methods can generally be divided into time-of-flight
measurements (often using echoes)910 or resonance based measurements1112. Unfortunately, both
methods ha
title: Staacks 2018 Simple Time of Flight Speed of Sound Smartphones

text:
time-of-flight
measurements (often using echoes)910 or resonance based measurements1112. Unfortunately, both
methods have their drawbacks. So far, time-of-flight measurement methods required students to
extract the time from an app that is not designed to give this information directly, often by analyzing
visual wave form representations of recorded audio signals, which can be difficult and too abstract
for younger students. This quickly becomes a distraction from the core experiment and can be
disproportionately time consuming. The resonance based experiments usually do not suffer from
these problems as there are many apps which directly show the frequency spectrum of an audio
recording and hence provide a numerical value of the peaks to work with.
title: Staacks 2018 Simple Time of Flight Speed of Sound Smartphones

text:
irectly show the frequency spectrum of an audio
recording and hence provide a numerical value of the peaks to work with. But these experiments
require a higher level of understanding because the students need to know stationary waves and
relate resonance frequencies to the geometry of the resonator in order to extract the speed of sound.
Our new experimental setup combines advantages of both methods by requiring only a minimum of
physics background while still offering a simple numeric result directly from the app on the
smartphone. This allows students to understand the principle of sound propagation and the speed of
sound by calculating their result as the simple ratio of distance over time. For this experiment we
use our free app "phyphox". To rea

text:
lating their result as the simple ratio of distance over time. For this experiment we
use our free app "phyphox". To reach as many students as possible, we try to ensure that all of its
features are available for the major operating systems if technically feasible for any device from
Android 4.0 and iOS 8. The free app is available from the respective app stores. It is specifically
designed for physics experiments in science education and offers access to the phone's sensors
along with unique features such as customizable data analysis and a simple method to remotely
access and control your experiment from a second device. For more information refer to
http://phyphox.org.

text:
Here, we use a specific data analysis tool of the app, called the "acoustic stopwatch" (Fig. 1). It uses
the microphone to listen for sound to trigger the stopwatch. As soon as the audio amplitude exceeds
a given threshold a time measurement is started. When the amplitude exceeds the threshold a
second time, the measurement stops and the time between the two acoustic events is shown.
Additionally, a minimum delay can be set to avoid unintentionally stopping the stopwatch with the
first sound event due to its duration or reverberation. This concept can be shown to the students
easily by clapping and letting them try out how the acoustic stopwatch reacts. If the stopwatch starts
without clapping or misses claps, it is usually sufficient to increase the
title: Staacks 2018 Simple Time of Flight Speed of Sound Smartphones

text:
tic stopwatch reacts. If the stopwatch starts
without clapping or misses claps, it is usually sufficient to increase the trigger threshold or to reduce
it, which is the only experimental configuration required.
The experiment is conducted by two students with a smartphone each. They place the phones at a
defined distance (for example 5 meters). Both students get their acoustic stopwatch ready and stand
next to one of the phones each (Fig. 2). Then the first student (A) generates a loud acoustic signal
(clapping, drums, popping balloons, etc.) to start the time measurement on both smartphones. Note,
that the phone B at the other end will start its measurement at a delay equal to the time ∆td it takes
for the sound to travel the distance d between both

text:
will start its measurement at a delay equal to the time ∆td it takes
for the sound to travel the distance d between both phones. Then, while both phones are running,
the second student (B) generates a second acoustic signal to stop both phones. Again, the distant

earlier by ∆td, now also stops later by ∆td. Therefore phone A measures a total time ∆tA equal to the
time ∆tB measured by phone B plus two times ∆td:
Therefore, we can get ∆td from the difference of both measured time intervals, resulting in the
following equation for the speed of sound:
The experimental results are surprisingly good. Since the microphone generates samples at a rate of
48 kHz, the theoretical temporal resolution is way below 1 ms. In practice, this is limited by finite
risetimes of actual acoustical events which are recorded differently by both phones due to the
attenuation over the distance. If you make sure that both phones and the

attenuation over the distance. If you make sure that both phones and the origins of both trigger
sounds are on a straight line and if you avoid wind, you can easily determine the speed of sound
over a distance of 5 meters to an uncertainty of 30 m/s (357 m/s for our setup), which is quite
accurate considering the simplicity of this experiment.

text:
马大猷先生(1915.3.1—2012.7.17) 是在国际上享有盛誉的声学家，是我国现代声学事业的重要开创者与
奠基人。在先生去世之后的十余年里，几乎每一届的国际声学大会(ICA)、国际噪声控制工程大会(Inter-
Noise) 和国际声学与振动大会(ICSV) 都会有专题的论文或者纪念专题(Special Session)，回顾或者发扬先生对
现代声学，特别是噪声控制领域做出的突出学术贡献。在2021 年的国际噪声控制工程大会上，专题回顾了噪
声控制工程领域7 篇有影响力的经典文章，马大猷先生创立的“微穿孔板宽带吸声理论”(1987) 与“矩形房间声
衰变理论”(1939) 均位列其中。马先生对我国声学事业的贡献更是具有开创性、引领性、前瞻性的意义，概括
而言，比较典型的工作体现在如下的几个方面。
1. 建筑声学与房间声学理论。马先生对房间声学的研究贯穿于他的整个学术生涯, 始于他的博士论文研
究, 直至他晚年关于房间直达声与混响声的分离表达。其中, 房间简正频率计算方法与房间声衰变是一个教
科书式的声学基础理论, 而人民大会堂万人礼堂的音质设计则是厅堂声学理论得到成功应用的典范。先生在
这方面的一系列工作, 为我国建筑声学的发展和应用奠定了坚实基础, 今天, 我国的厅堂与房间声学设计有方
法、有技术、有手段、有人才, 一般大型的厅堂音质都控制得很好, 莫不得益于此。展望未来, 教室与小型会议
室、餐厅等量大面广的中小型公共房间的音质设计建造、改造仍面临许多突出的问题, 亟待从建设标准、设计
准则、测试控制技术等方面加大工作力度。
2. 环境声学与噪声控制技术。是马先生率先在国内提出噪声是一种环境污染的概念, 应该与大气污染、
水污染、固体废弃物污染并列为四大污染源之一, 而且是唯一值得高
title: TianJing 2025 沿着马大猷先生开拓的方向不断前进

准则、测试控制技术等方面加大工作力度。
2. 环境声学与噪声控制技术。是马先生率先在国内提出噪声是一种环境污染的概念, 应该与大气污染、
水污染、固体废弃物污染并列为四大污染源之一, 而且是唯一值得高度重视的物理污染, 影响深远。他亲自领
导开展噪声测试调查, 建立环境噪声污染评价标准, 推动并亲自参与制定国家环境噪声污染防治条例以及第
一部环境噪声污染防治法。他创新性地提出微穿孔板吸声材料和高压排放小孔消声器, 理论建树享誉世界,
而且得到十分广泛的推广应用, 使我国的噪声控制技术走在国际前列。直至今日, 国际上的声学超材料、声学
“黑洞”等热门研究方向仍可以在此找到活水源头。为响应党中央“还自然以宁静、和谐、美丽”的号召, 贯彻落
实新版噪声法, 中国科学院声学研究所提出了“宁静中国”建设科技行动倡议, 是积极面对新时代新形势下的
噪声污染新挑战新问题, 加快噪声机理研究和关键技术攻关应用的步伐, 疏通噪声控制技术转移转化的途径,
使我国的噪声控制水平能够适应经济社会发展和人民生活水平不断提高的大趋势。
3. 强声学与非线性声学理论。马先生紧密围绕国家在航空航天领域的战略需求, 率先创造条件, 领导开
展强声学研究。他最早组织研发成功万瓦级气动扬声器, 建造了声级120~180 dB 的强声行波管、驻波管与混
响室, 并开展了航空航天材料的声疲劳试验及应用服务, 随后指导有关行业建立了自己的试验室, 培养建设了
自己的研发与应用人才力量。先生在1990 年代后期开始重视系统的非线性声学理论研究, 指导完成了深入
的实验观察, 从理论上揭示了强声能量由基频向谐波的非线性转移、耗散与阻断机理, 为高强度纯声的产生和
保持提供了理论依据。随着高超声速技术与工

source: TianJing_2025_沿着马大猷先生开拓的方向不断前进.pdf
text:
的研发与应用人才力量。先生在1990 年代后期开始重视系统的非线性声学理论研究, 指导完成了深入
的实验观察, 从理论上揭示了强声能量由基频向谐波的非线性转移、耗散与阻断机理, 为高强度纯声的产生和
保持提供了理论依据。随着高超声速技术与工业高声强技术的发展应用, 非线性声学过程及其控制仍具有十
分重要的基础性意义。
4. 语言声学与语音编码技术。早在1958 年, 马先生就提出开展人机对话和智能计算机研究的建议, 亲自
组织进行了汉语语音分析、识别和合成的研究, 1961 年完成了10 个元音的识别, 是早期语音识别研究的重要
里程碑。他指导研究生在国内率先实现微机特定人口语指令识别系统, 获得国际大奖, 走在世界人机对话前
列。他领导的语言合成研究先后研制出三代声码器, 为我国专用通信事业做出了重要贡献。目前, 从语音、语
言研究发展出来的大语言模型、深度学习等等上升为关系国家前途命运的人工智能核心算法, 意义十分重
大。语义与思维的底层逻辑成为基础算法竞争的焦点, 而有限资源单体的智能及其与云端的协同则决定了
AI 应用的能力边界。马先生所开创的言语物理机理研究以及机器编码处理技术, 在理解人类智能的发展脉
络, 开发更加高效、绿色、低成本的AI 算法等方面, 仍然具有基础性、方法性的指导意义。

5. 次声学与大气声学理论。1960 年代, 马先生紧扣国家战略需求, 率先提出开展次声监测和远程大气声
传播研究的建议, 并组织研发成功次声传感器与大范围的次声监测分析系统, 对核爆炸等人类行为与火山爆
发、地震、台风等自然灾害产生的次声波在大气中的传播进行了系统的理论与实验研究, 获得了重要的数据
与一系列成果。1984 年获得中国科学院重大科技成果一等奖。进入21 世纪, 国际核军控形势日益严峻, 大气
变暖与人类对自然环境的无节制开发等造成的极端天气与地质灾害频发, 次声作为有效的实时甚至先兆性的
监测手段, 配合以日益先进的AI 算法分析, 必将发挥越来越重要的作用。
除了以上这些学术上的开创性工作之外, 马先生还在我国声学领域的学会、学报、声学技术标准化以及
人才教育等方面身体力行, 建树颇丰, 奠定了很好的发展基础。
进入新的时代, 吾等后辈当饮水思源, 以先生为榜样, 爱国奉献, 开拓创新, 为实现中华民族伟大复兴的中
国梦做出新的更大贡献。
谨此纪念马大猷先生诞辰110 周年。

of Colladon’s nineteenth century experiments
Armand Wirgin ∗

Abstract
In 1827, Colladon carried out a series of experiments in Lac Leman (Lake Geneva, Switzer-
land) to measure the speed of sound in water. The purpose of our contribution is to treat this
measurement as an inverse problem, and show, by theory how to solve the latter. It is thus
revealed under what circumstances it is legitimate to employ the time-of-ﬂight scheme underly-
ing the Colladon experiments and how to bypass this scheme in order to fully account for the
temporal and geometric characteristics of the source (of sound), the temporal characteristics of
the rece

Introduction
The measurement of the bulk velocity of sound in various kinds of homogeneous media (solid,
liquid, gaseous) has been a subject of research for centuries (Baskevitch, 2008). It became quickly
known (the non-inﬁnitesimal time delay between a vocalized sound and its echo in a mountainous
environment being a readily-measurable experience to anybody) that sound propagates with a
velocity that is ﬁnite (contrary to that of light which was at ﬁrst thought to be inﬁnite, and later
to be ’very large’), and therefore susceptible of being measured by quite simple means (henceforth
termed the kinematic method), usually deriving from the inversion of the formula ∆x = v∆t, v the
velocity of sound, ∆x the known distance between two points (usually t
title: Wirgin 2017 Colladon Sturm velocity of sound in water history

text:
from the inversion of the formula ∆x = v∆t, v the
velocity of sound, ∆x the known distance between two points (usually the point of sound emission
and another point (of reception), more or less far from the ﬁrst point, and ∆t the time it takes for
the sound to propagate from the ﬁrst to second points. In this formula, ∆x and ∆t are observed
quantities, from which v is retrieved by inversion via the formula v = ∆x/∆t. The same formula
also reveals: i) the fact that if it is possible to observe only rather large ∆t then ∆x must be chosen
to be correspondingly large, ii) the accuracy of the retrieval of v depends heavily on the accuracy
of the observation of ∆x which can be low for large ∆x, iii) likewise, the accuracy of the retrieval
of v depends on t
title: Wirgin 2017 Colladon Sturm velocity of sound in water history

text:
y
of the observation of ∆x which can be low for large ∆x, iii) likewise, the accuracy of the retrieval
of v depends on the accuracy of the observation of ∆t which can be low for small ∆t (whence the
interest in disposing of reliable means (e.g., clocks, watches, etc. (Derham, 1696; Derham, 1708))
for measuring time. Finally, it must be stressed that v cannot be observed directly (contrary to
∆x and ∆t, but rather that its measurement is an inverse problem employing data related to a
distance and interval of time.
There exists another approach to the problem of the measurement of v, namely from ﬁrst
(physical) principles. The ﬁrst to do this was Newton who related the bulk velocity of sound to
the density and compressibility of the material in which i
title: Wirgin 2017 Colladon Sturm velocity of sound in water history

text:
do this was Newton who related the bulk velocity of sound to
the density and compressibility of the material in which it propagates. This is again an inverse
problem in which the data is now connected to observations of density and compressibility.
Newton found that the v in air retrieved by the two methods diﬀered considerably and all
his rather contrived attempts to account for this diﬀerence failed. (Bruce, 2012; Westfall, 1973)
This opened up a new avenue of research on the validity of Newton’s formula, focused mainly on
the velocity of sound in air. It led to Laplace’s ﬁnding (Finn,1964; Roberts,2008) that Newton’s
formula takes no account of the inﬂuence of the heat generated in the air by the compression of
this gas.
While most of the researc
title: Wirgin 2017 Colladon Sturm velocity of sound in water history

text:
es no account of the inﬂuence of the heat generated in the air by the compression of
this gas.
While most of the research (both theoretical and experimental) on the velocity of sound centered
on that of air (Lenihan,1952) and other gases, Colladon and Sturm (Colladon & Sturm, 1827a;
Colladon & Sturm, 1827b; Colladon & Sturm, 1827c; Colladon, 1837; Colladon, 1893) chose to
focus their attention on liquids, the most common of which is water. They did this ﬁrstly by the
physical method based on data observed (by them) connected with density, compressibility and
the heat generated during compression of the ﬂuid, and secondly (after concluding that Newton’s
formula was correct in pure water since the heat problem is of negligible inﬂuence on the propagati
title: Wirgin 2017 Colladon Sturm velocity of sound in water history

text:
luding that Newton’s
formula was correct in pure water since the heat problem is of negligible inﬂuence on the propagation
of sound therein) by the kinematic method.
The remarkable work of Colladon and Sturm is of experimental nature, with much attention
given to detail, especially in their experiments related to the kinematic method of speciﬁc interest
herein. Although they made many eﬀorts to eliminate all sources of error (in the kinematic method),
it appeared to us that they were either not aware, or underestimated the importance, of two
problems having to do with the spectrum and geometric support of the source of pulse-like sound
they propagated in the water and the inﬂuence of observational error concerning the onset time of

the sound pulse. Taking into account these factors, as well as others concerning the inﬂuence of
the far-ﬁeld and paraxial region assumptions on retrieval error, will be the subject of the second
part of this investigation.
Colladon & Sturm’x publication was written in french and therefore not known to a large part
of the scientiﬁc community. This is unfortunate since their work gives a good glimpse of some
of the key issues that physicists wrestled with during the 17th to 19th centuries. Other than its
historical interest, the work of Colladon & Sturm has a sort of esthetic value that derives from the
considerable ingeniosity employed in devising and carrying out the experiments.

1.1
Beudant and Colladon
In his textbook on physics (Beudant, 1824); section Liquids in motion, subsection Vibratory
motion), Beudant alludes very vaguely to his experiments on the speed of sound in water. It is
probable that Colladon read this book and later interrogated Beudant on details of his experiment.
Thus, the Beudant experiments can reasonably be thought to have inspired Colladon’s own 1826
experiments in Lake Leman.
1.1.1
Beudant’s book
On page 296 of his book (Beudant, 1824), Beudant writes;
Liquids are able to vibrate when they are in contact with a body to which such motion has been
procured. In eﬀect, if one places water in a standing glass, and he
title: Wirgin 2017 Colladon Sturm velocity of sound in water history

text:
in contact with a body to which such motion has been
procured. In eﬀect, if one places water in a standing glass, and he passes his ﬁnger on the edge of
the said glass to produce a sound, one immediately observes that the surface of the liquid is marked
by wrinkles that move from the circumference to the center.
The vibratory property of liquids is also proven by the ease with which they propagate the
sound produced at an arbitrary point in their volume. If, being submerged in water, one strikes a
bell in the liquid, the intensity of the perceived sound will be much larger than if he was in air; the
sound, by its intensity, is even very uncomfortable to the ear. One ﬁnds here another example of
the providential goodness of the Creator, who did not gi

text:
very uncomfortable to the ear. One ﬁnds here another example of
the providential goodness of the Creator, who did not give to the hearing organs of ﬁshes all the
development that can be observed in the majority of terrestrial animals.
The ability of transmitting sound is not the same in all liquids; it seems, from various ex-
periments conducted in Turin by Mr. P´erolle, that it is directly related to the speciﬁc weights
[densities].
Mr. Laplace, by speciﬁc considerations, based on the compression of which water is capable,
gives the ﬁgure of 1526 m/s for the speed of sound in rainwater, and 1621 m/s in seawater. I already

Colladon’s probable inspiration
Here is an excerpt from section 3-1 of (Colladon, 1837) entitled Vitesse du son dans les liquides:
The only experiment carried out until now on the velocity of sound in a liquid body is due to
M. Beudant [F.S. Beudant, 1813]; it was done in sea water, near Marseille, not many years ago.
Here are some details of this experiment that this scientist agreed to communicate to us. The two
observers, separated one from the other by a known distance, had synchronized watches that gave
the same time together; at an instant decided beforehand, the person who was supposed to produce
the sound raised a ﬂag an
title: Wirgin 2017 Colladon Sturm velocity of sound in water history

text:
e same time together; at an instant decided beforehand, the person who was supposed to produce
the sound raised a ﬂag and simultaneously struck a small immersed bell. The observer situated
elsewhere was accompanied by an aid who swam near his boat, heard the sound, and indicated
by some sign the moment of its arrival. Thus was obtained the measure of the time taken by the
sound to travel from one place to the other: this measurement was not rigorously exact, because
the person in the water could not give his signal at precisely the instant that he heard the sound.
M. Beaudant concluded from his experiments that the velocity of sound in seawater is 1500 m/s;
but as his several experiments led to substantial diﬀerences, he gave this result only as an a
title: Wirgin 2017 Colladon Sturm velocity of sound in water history

text:
in seawater is 1500 m/s;
but as his several experiments led to substantial diﬀerences, he gave this result only as an average.
It is probable that the real velocity does not diﬀer substantially from this average, which is in fair
agreement with theory. But, in order to make this comparison in a more certain manner, it would
have been necessary to have a perfectly exact measurement, and, in addition, determine rigorously
the density and the compressibility of the liquid at the very temperature of the experiment.
The water of a lake seemed to us to be the most appropriate for giving immediately the velocity
of sound in pure water.

Introduction [and Experiments on the compressibility of the liquids]
This memoir is divided into four parts.
In the ﬁrst part, we discuss the experiments relative to the measurement of the compressibility of
ﬂuids; the second part has to do with experiments on the release of caloric [heat] that accompanies
compression; in the third part we seek to ﬁnd out if the pressure has an inﬂuence on the electric
conductivity of these substances; ﬁnally, in the fourth part we give a measure of the velocity of
sound in fresh water obtained by our experiments, and we compare it with the theory.
The ﬁrst experiments on the compression of ﬂuids were made at the end of the 17th century
by some Florentine physicists. At that time the discoveries of Galileo and

by some Florentine physicists. At that time the discoveries of Galileo and Torricelli had attracted
the attention of scientists doing research in experimental physics. Mariotte [(Mariotte, 1717), but
also (Boyle, 1662)] had already recognized the law of the compressibility of gases. The members
of the el Cimento academy, working together on a series of experiments concerning the properties
of imponderable solids and ﬂuids, rightly judged that water should be compressible, because it is
able to transmit sound, made several tries to measure this reduction in volume.
In 1761, the physicist John Canton [(Canton, 1761)], returned to this important question.
Having ﬁrst recognized the compressibility of water, h

text:
ohn Canton [(Canton, 1761)], returned to this important question.
Having ﬁrst recognized the compressibility of water, he undertook precise experiments to measure
this compressibility. His work was not limited to water, since he showed that several other liquids
had, like water, the property of being compressible [(Canton, 1764)]. His experimental method,
which since then has been perfected by Mr. Oersted [(Oersted,1823)], consists in compressing the
liquids in instruments resembling thermometers, composed of a large capacity bulb, surmounted
by a capillary tube opened at its upper extremity.
Oersted’s experiments on water, at constant temperature, did not exceed compressions of six
atmospheres, so that there remained to try larger compressions, not

atmospheres, so that there remained to try larger compressions, not only on water, but on several
other liquids of diﬀerent densities, and to observe for each of them the inﬂuence of the temperature
on the compressibility, as well as to ﬁnd out if heat is released due to their compression.
Our instrument for determining the compressibility of liquids is composed of two distinct parts,
one of which measures the reduction in volume of the liquid which is submitted to a certain pressure,
while the other part quantiﬁes the compression. The precision of the results depends on the exact
and simultaneous observation of these two quantities.

The phenomena connected with the heat resulting from the compression of substances have,

The phenomena connected with the heat resulting from the compression of substances have,
during the last few years, attracted the attention of several geometers [theoretical physicists and
applied mathematicians] and physicists [experimental and applied physicists]. The understanding
of these phenomena is connected with the most important questions in physics, and could lead
to consequences of great interest concerning the very nature of heat and the relations that exist
between this ﬂuid and the diﬀerent substances.
These researches have acquired increased importance for the geometers from the moment that
Mr. Laplace demonstrated its application to the theory of sound, and proved that by taking into
account the heat released by the comp
title: Wirgin 2017 Colladon Sturm velocity of sound in water history

text:
emonstrated its application to the theory of sound, and proved that by taking into
account the heat released by the compression of air, one is able to reconcile the mathematical
formula for [the velocity of] sound with the results furnished by experiment.
The phenomena of the release of heat by the compression of gases are now practically elucidated,
thanks to the work of Mr. Gay-Lussac, Mr. Cl´ement, Mr. Desormes [(Gay-Lussac,1802; Clement
& Desormes, 1819)], and to the recent research of Mr. de La Rive and Mr. Marcet [(De La Rive &

The retrieval of the velocity of sound is an inverse wave propagation problem which can be
formulated as follows:
i) trace a line from the location of a pulse-like sound-emitting source Ps to the location Pr of a
hypothetical, rather distant (from the source location) receiver,
ii) place two identical receivers, one at

text:
tion Pr of a
hypothetical, rather distant (from the source location) receiver,
ii) place two identical receivers, one at a point P1 not too distant laterally from the line and
longitudinally from Ps, and the other at a point P2 not too distant laterally from the line and
longitudinally from Pr,
iii) observe the coordinates of the two points P1 and P2,
iv) register the sound signals at these two points and note the time instants at which the same
remarkable feature, such as the maximum, of the pulse occurs,
v) either by comparison of the registered pulses at the two locations, or from the measured time
interval between the occurrence of the remarkable feature in the two signals, retrieve, using the
coordinate information of the receiver locations, the

coordinate information of the receiver locations, the velocity v of the medium in which the sound
propagates, under the assumptions that this medium is a homogeneous ﬂuid of inﬁnite spatial
extent, the support of the source is line-like, and the spectrum and onset time of the sound pulse
is known (note that in Colladon’s experiments in Lac Leman, these assumptions were made, but
no account was taken of a possible lack of information concerning the pulse spectrum and of the
onset time of the pulse).

Several features emerge from these curves:
1. the numerical results conﬁrm the TOF theoretical prediction that uncertainty of β indeed
leads to error in the retrieval of v, with it even being possible to obtain a retrieved v that is
larger than the true v; in fact the numerically-retrieved velocity is larger (smaller) than the
true velocity v for β′ > β (β′ < β respectively), as predicted by the theoretical TOF analysis,
2. the two schemes (TOF and FWI) give the same results for large x, so that the TOF scheme
can be used without hesitation for the retrieval of v far enough from the source (although one
has to go farther away the larger is the uncertainty of β),
3. the retrievals are not aﬀected by the choice of pulse width (controlled by α−1), at le

text:
rger is the uncertainty of β),
3. the retrievals are not aﬀected by the choice of pulse width (controlled by α−1), at least far from
the source and when there is no uncertainty concerning α, in agreement with the theoretical
TOF analysis,
4. whatever the uncertainty of β, the farther the receiver is from the source, the smaller is the
retrieval error, a fact also predicted by the theoretical TOF analysis, and which explains why
it is important to acquire signal data as far as possible from the source in order to retrieve v.

2.11
More accurate schemes for the retrieval of v
The retrievals of v observed in sect. 2.9 are unreliable in that; i) they employ expressions of
the ﬁeld which depend on the satisfaction of the far-ﬁeld and paraxial region constraints, and ii)
the TOF method of retrieval is not generally applicable unless the ﬁeld can be approximated by
the far-ﬁeld paraxial region expression. The
title: Wirgin 2017 Colladon Sturm velocity of sound in water history

text:
trieval is not generally applicable unless the ﬁeld can be approximated by
the far-ﬁeld paraxial region expression. The way to avoid these problems is to discard the TOF
scheme in favor of a full-wave inversion (FWI) method appealing to a data simulation model (when
the data is simulated) and a retrieval model whose ingredients do not rely on far-ﬁeld and paraxial
approximations so as to be able to account accurately for all the physical and geometric factors
that contribute to the measured or synthetic data.
3
Conclusion
It may be asked why Colladon chose such a large distance (14km) between the source and the
receiver. He estimated that the absolute error in observing ∆t was 0.5 s. This is 0.056 of 9 s
(the time it took sound to travel 14000 m), bu
title: Wirgin 2017 Colladon Sturm velocity of sound in water history

text:
d that the absolute error in observing ∆t was 0.5 s. This is 0.056 of 9 s
(the time it took sound to travel 14000 m), but 0.25 of ∼2 s (i.e., the time it took for sound to
41
title: Wirgin 2017 Colladon Sturm velocity of sound in water history

text:
travel 2500 m). This means that the relative error on observing ∆t is about ﬁve times larger for
the shorter distance than for the larger distance (assuming that the absolute error on ∆t is a half
second in both cases, i.e., independent of the distance). But this choice of larger ∆x to obtain a
smaller relative error on ∆t was risky because the probability of the sound encountering bottom
obstacles, inhomogeneities, temperature variations in the water of a natural environment are all
the greater, the longer the distance traveled by the sound.
Colladon was unaware of the fact that long distances and paraxial conditions are, in fact neces-
sary for him to have been able to employ the TOF scheme on which these conditions are based. Nor
did he know that
title: Wirgin 2017 Colladon Sturm velocity of sound in water history

text:
eces-
sary for him to have been able to employ the TOF scheme on which these conditions are based. Nor
did he know that ignorance of the shape of his pulse is permissible if the conditions for employing
the TOF scheme are satisﬁed. Above all, Colladon did not dispose of a mathematical model of his
experiment, which is what we proposed to provide herein.
This model would have told him that his TOF method can only be applied in speciﬁc cir-
cumstances and that if the latter are not satisﬁed, the TOF measurement result is in error. He
could have saved some trouble (and further sources of error due to the variability of the physical
properties of a large-scale medium) by choosing a smaller distance between the source and receiver
and treating the inverse
title: Wirgin 2017 Colladon Sturm velocity of sound in water history

text:
perties of a large-scale medium) by choosing a smaller distance between the source and receiver
and treating the inverse problem via the FWI (which also enables the evaluation of the error on
v due to uncertainty on the onset time of the pulse as well as on other experimental parameter
uncertainties.
Nevertheless, the Colladon experiments on the kinematic method for the measurement of the
velocity of sound were very ingenious (all the more so than they were carried out without the help of
any electronic or even electrical devices; more recent experimental methods for such measurements
can be found in publications such as (Papadakis,1967; Del Grosso & Mader, 1972))).
We chose not to analyze or comment on the the other aspects of the publications of Co

& Sturn because they speak for themselves and deal with matters that are outside the scope of
our contribution which concerned the ﬁrst method (in the terminology of our Introduction) for the
measurement of the velocity of sound. We hope that our translation of the material concerning
the second (physical principles) method (as well as that of the ﬁrst method) will be of use to
those interested in the history of science, particularly those aspects of which deal with the intense
scientiﬁc activity centered on the mechanics and thermodynamics of deformable media that took

# 声速四种方法 Julia 综合可视化实验方案

## 一、实验概述

本实验把“回声法测量声速”“双麦克风时间差法”“示波器相位差法”和“驻波法测量声速”整合到同一个 Julia/GLMakie 程序中。四个模式共享同一个真实声速参数，但分别观察脉冲往返时间、双通道到达时间差、连续波相位差和驻波波节间距。

统一界面包含三个同步区域：

1. 左图显示声波的空间传播或驻波瞬时形状；
2. 中图显示原始信号、含噪测量信号或入射波与反射波；
3. 右图显示当前方法的分析结果；
4. 下方给出理论量、测量量、估计声速和相对误差；
5. 参数改变时显示“正在计算...”，计算结束后恢复为“就绪”。

## 二、运行方法

在本方案目录中运行：

```powershell
julia --project=. run.jl
```

首次运行会自动安装 `GLMakie`。如果环境已经安装完成，可跳过依赖检查：

```powershell
julia --project=. run.jl --no-instantiate
```

模型自检和无交互界面测试：

```powershell
julia --project=. run.jl --no-instantiate --self-test
julia --project=. run.jl --no-instantiate --smoke-test
```

## 三、统一界面与参数

顶部四个按钮用于切换测量方法。不同方法只显示与当前实验有关的控件。

顶部四个按钮用于切换测量方法。不同方法只显示与当前实验有关的控件。

| 参数 | 作用 | 适用模式 |
|---|---|---|
| 真实声速 `v` | 生成理论信号并作为误差比较基准 | 全部 |
| 距离 `d` 或管长 `L` | 墙面距离、麦克风间距或驻波管长度 | 全部 |
| 频率 `f` | 决定连续波波长与相位累积 | 相位法、驻波法 |
| 信噪比 `SNR` | 控制测量信号中的随机噪声 | 回声法、双麦克风法、相位法 |
| 采样率 `fs` | 决定时间差的数字化分辨率 | 回声法、双麦克风法 |
| 反射系数 `r` | 控制回声强度或驻波完整程度 | 回声法、驻波法 |
| 入射夹角 `θ` | 修正麦克风基线的有效投影距离 | 双麦克风法 |
| 完整周期数 `n` | 对包裹相位进行相位展开 | 相位法 |
| 波节间隔数 `q` | 模拟跨越多个波节进行测量 | 驻波法 |

“传播/振动进程”滑块可手动观察任意时刻；“播放”按钮用于连续演示；“重置”恢复默认参数；“导出 PNG + CSV”保存当前界面和数值数据。

前三种方法采用三面板同步播放：左图推进空间传播，中图推进信号采集，右图推进数据分析。淡色曲线表示完整参考结果，彩色曲线表示当前进程已经采集或分析的部分，游标表示当前时刻或当前位置。驻波法的左图和中图显示随时间变化的瞬时波形，右图保留不随时间改变的振幅包络。

## 四、模式一：回声法

### 4.1 原理

## 四、模式一：回声法

### 4.1 原理

声源与墙面的距离为 `d`，脉冲传播到墙面后返回，总路程为 `2d`。若直达脉冲与回声脉冲之间的时间差为 `Δt`，则

$$
v=\frac{2d}{\Delta t}.
$$

程序严格按照采样间隔 `1/fs` 生成两个高斯脉冲，并在各自的时间窗中自动寻找峰值。含噪信号可写成

$$
s(t)=p(t-t_0)+r\,p(t-t_0-\Delta t)+n(t).
$$

### 4.2 可视化读数

- 左图的三个绿色点依次表示声源、传播中的波前和墙面；
- 中图蓝线是直达脉冲，红线是回声，黄线是含噪测量信号；
- 两条虚线标出自动识别的峰值到达时刻；
- 右图绘制 `2d-vΔt` 直线，当前测量点偏离直线的程度反映采样和噪声误差。

### 4.3 建议实验

1. 固定 `v=343 m/s`、`fs=48000 Hz`，逐渐增大墙面距离，观察两峰间距；
2. 降低反射系数，找出仍能稳定识别回声的最小值；
3. 固定距离并降低采样率，记录估计声速的阶梯式变化；
4. 降低信噪比，观察峰值误判和误差增大的过程；
5. 记录多组 `2d` 与 `Δt`，验证直线斜率等于声速。

## 五、模式二：双麦克风时间差法

### 5.1 原理

两个麦克风间距为 `d`。声波传播方向与麦克风连线夹角为 `θ` 时，有效传播距离为 `d cosθ`：

$$
v=\frac{d\cos\theta}{\Delta t}.
$$

五、模式二：双麦克风时间差法

### 5.1 原理

两个麦克风间距为 `d`。声波传播方向与麦克风连线夹角为 `θ` 时，有效传播距离为 `d cosθ`：

$$
v=\frac{d\cos\theta}{\Delta t}.
$$

程序计算归一化离散互相关：

$$
R_{xy}[k]=
\frac{\sum_i x[i]y[i+k]}
{\sqrt{\sum_i x^2[i]\sum_i y^2[i+k]}}.
$$

最大相关峰对应的整数采样点偏移为 `kmax`，因此

$$
\Delta t=\frac{k_{\max}}{f_s}.
$$

### 5.2 可视化读数

- 左图显示两个麦克风、麦克风基线和移动波前；
- 中图显示两路同步采样信号及各自到达时刻；
- 右图显示完整互相关曲线，黄点标记最大相关峰；
- 结果区同时显示投影距离、相关峰时延、估计声速和相对误差。

### 5.3 建议实验

1. 改变麦克风间距，比较时延和速度估计的稳定性；
2. 将入射夹角从 `0°` 增大到 `60°`，验证 `cosθ` 修正；
3. 比较不同采样率下相关峰的横坐标量化误差；
4. 降低信噪比，观察主相关峰下降和旁峰增强；
5. 将结果与回声法比较，解释单程距离和往返距离的区别。

## 六、模式三：示波器相位差法

### 6.1 原理

两个位置的同频正弦信号为

$$
y_1(t)=A\sin(2\pi ft),
$$

$$
y_2(t)=A\sin(2\pi ft-\Delta\phi).
$$

传播相位与距离满足

$$
\Delta\phi_{\mathrm{total}}=\frac{2\pi fd}{v}.
$$

$$

$$
y_2(t)=A\sin(2\pi ft-\Delta\phi).
$$

传播相位与距离满足

$$
\Delta\phi_{\mathrm{total}}=\frac{2\pi fd}{v}.
$$

示波器只能直接得到 `0` 到 `2π` 范围内的包裹相位。若传播距离包含 `n` 个完整波长，则

$$
v=\frac{2\pi fd}{2\pi n+\Delta\phi_{\mathrm{wrapped}}}.
$$

程序通过复数投影估计两通道相位差，并允许手动选择完整周期数 `n`。

### 6.2 可视化读数

- 左图显示行波以及两个麦克风的空间位置；
- 中图模拟示波器双通道，水平位移对应相位差；
- 右图的锯齿曲线显示相位每增加 `360°` 后重新折返；
- 结果区同时显示包裹相位、真实完整周期数和当前 `n` 对应的速度。

### 6.3 建议实验

1. 缓慢增加麦克风间距，观察包裹相位的周期性折返；
2. 故意选择错误的完整周期数，比较估计声速的巨大偏差；
3. 降低频率，观察波长增大后相位歧义减少；
4. 增加频率，比较相位灵敏度提高和周期歧义加重之间的权衡；
5. 先用双麦克风时间差法粗测声速，再据此确定相位法的整数周期。

## 七、模式四：驻波法

### 7.1 原理

程序采用入射波和反射波

$$
y_i=A\sin(kx-\omega t),
$$

$$
y_r=rA\sin(kx+\omega t).
$$

当 `r=1` 时，两者合成为理想驻波：

$$
y=2A\sin(kx)\cos(\omega t).
$$

相邻波节间距为 `λ/2`。若跨越 `q` 个波节间隔测得总距离 `Dq`，则

$$

当 `r=1` 时，两者合成为理想驻波：

$$
y=2A\sin(kx)\cos(\omega t).
$$

相邻波节间距为 `λ/2`。若跨越 `q` 个波节间隔测得总距离 `Dq`，则

$$
v=f\lambda=\frac{2fD_q}{q}.
$$

### 7.2 可视化读数

- 左图显示驻波瞬时形状，绿色点标记理论波节；
- 中图同时显示入射波、反射波和合成波；
- 右图显示振幅包络，反射系数小于 1 时波节不再严格为零；
- 结果区给出波长、相邻波节间距、跨越多个间隔的总长度和估计声速。

### 7.3 建议实验

1. 拖动振动进程，验证波节位置不随时间移动；
2. 改变频率，验证相邻波节间距与频率成反比；
3. 将反射系数逐步降低，观察不完全驻波的最小振幅；
4. 比较测量一个波节间隔和多个波节间隔的读数方法；
5. 调整管长，使末端落在波节、波腹或中间位置，讨论边界条件。

## 八、四种方法的综合比较

| 方法 | 直接观测量 | 主要优点 | 主要限制 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 回声法 | 往返时间 | 装置简单、空间过程直观 | 近距离脉冲可能重叠 |
| 双麦克风法 | 单程时间差 | 易于自动化，可用互相关抗噪 | 依赖同步采样和方向修正 |
| 相位差法 | 包裹相位 | 对微小位移灵敏 | 存在完整周期多值性 |
| 驻波法 | 波节间距 | 波长可直接可视化 | 依赖稳定反射和波节判定 |

综合演示时建议先用回声法建立“路程除以时间”的概念，再用双麦克风法展示数字信号处理，随后用相位差法讨论周期多值性，最后用驻波法把时间测量转换为空间波长测量。

# 声速测量的可视化演示题目

## 一、报告概述

声速测量既可以展示声波的传播过程，也可以联系波长、频率、相位差、驻波、共鸣和数字信号处理等内容。通过动画、实时波形、数据曲线和误差图，可以把难以直接观察的声波传播过程转化为直观的实验现象。

本报告整理适合制作 Python、网页或交互式物理实验的声速测量题目，并给出相应的实验原理、可视化内容和拓展问题。

## 二、回声法测量声速

### 题目示例

**利用回声时间差测量空气中的声速。**

### 实验原理

在距离障碍物 (d) 处发出声音，声音到达障碍物后反射回来。测量发声和接收到回声之间的时间间隔 Δt，可得：

$$
v=\frac{2d}{\Delta t}
$$

其中 (2d) 是声音往返传播的总路程。

### 可视化设计

- 用声源、障碍物和波纹表示声音的传播与反射；
- 实时显示传播距离、传播时间和计算出的声速；
- 同步绘制发声信号和回声信号的波形；
- 用标记线显示两个波峰之间的时间差。

### 可研究的问题

- 障碍物距离增加时，回声时间是否成正比增加？
- 距离太近时，为什么难以听到清晰的回声？
- 温度、风速和障碍物表面对结果有什么影响？

### 实验特点

原理简单，适合入门演示。使用录音设备或计算机检测时间差，通常比人工计时准确。

## 三、双麦克风时间差法

### 题目示例

**基于双麦克风时间延迟的声速测量。**

### 实验原理

将两个麦克风相距 (d)，声音先到达第一个麦克风，再到达第二个麦克风。若两个信号的到达时间差为 Δt，则：

$$
v=\frac{d}{\Delta t}
$$

界面可以分为三个区域：

### 可视化设计

界面可以分为三个区域：

1. 声源和两个麦克风的空间示意图；
2. 麦克风 1 和麦克风 2 的实时波形；
3. 到达时间、时间差和声速计算结果。

还可以通过滑块调节麦克风间距、声源频率、入射角和噪声强度。

### 数字信号处理

可使用互相关函数寻找两个信号的时间延迟：

$$
R_{xy}(\tau)=\int x(t)y(t+\tau)\,dt
$$

互相关函数最大值对应的 τ，就是两个信号之间的时间差。

### 可研究的问题

- 麦克风距离增大后，测量精度是否提高？
- 白噪声会如何影响相关峰？
- 采样频率对时间差测量有什么影响？
- 声音传播方向改变后，时间差如何变化？

### 实验特点

适合物理竞赛和编程项目，能够结合波动理论、数字信号处理、曲线拟合和误差分析。

## 四、示波器相位差法

### 题目示例

**利用双通道示波器测量声速。**

### 实验原理

两个麦克风接入示波器的两个通道。设麦克风间距为 (d)，时间差为 Δt，则：

$$
v=\frac{d}{\Delta t}
$$

若声波频率为 (f)，相位差为 Δφ，则：

$$
\frac{\Delta t}{T}=\frac{\Delta\varphi}{2\pi},\qquad T=\frac{1}{f}
$$

因此：

$$
v=\frac{2\pi f d}{\Delta\varphi}
$$

### 可视化设计

显示两列正弦波：

$$

$$

### 可研究的问题

- 距离增加一个波长时，两个信号是否恢复相同相位？
- 相位差超过 (2\pi) 后为什么会出现相位折返？
- 为什么一次相位差测量不能确定传播了多少个完整波长？
- 如何通过多次改变距离消除相位周期性带来的歧义？

## 五、利用李萨如图形测量声速

### 题目示例

**基于李萨如图形的声波相位差测量。**

### 实验原理

将两路同频声波信号分别接入示波器的 (X) 轴和 (Y) 轴：

$$
x=A\sin(\omega t)
$$

$$
y=B\sin(\omega t+\varphi)
$$

不同相位差会形成不同的图形：

- Δφ = 0：正向直线；
- Δφ = π：反向直线；
- Δφ = π/2：椭圆或圆；
- 其他相位差：倾斜椭圆。

### 可视化设计

同时显示两个麦克风、两路波形、李萨如图形、相位差和声速数值。改变麦克风间距时，图形应经历直线、椭圆、圆和反向直线等变化。

### 可研究的问题

- 李萨如图形为什么能反映相位差？
- 为什么相同图形可能对应多个不同的传播距离？
- 如何结合麦克风间距和波长确定真实相位？
- 频率改变后，图形的稳定性是否发生变化？

## 六、空气柱共鸣法

### 题目示例

**利用空气柱共鸣测量空气中的声速。**

### 实验原理

对于一端封闭、一端开口的管，当空气柱长度满足共鸣条件时，振幅明显增大：

$$
L_1=\frac{\lambda}{4},\qquad L_2=\frac{3\lambda}{4}
$$

相邻共鸣长度之差为：

$$
L_2-L_1=\frac{\lambda}{2}
$$

所以：

$$
\lambda=2(L_2-L_1),\qquad v=f\lambda
$$

### 可视化设计

- 用小圆点表示管内空气质点；
- 共鸣时让质点振幅明显增大；
- 显示波节、波腹和空气柱长度；
- 拖动活塞改变空气柱长度；
- 绘制振幅随管长变化的曲线 (A(L))。

### 可研究的问题

- 为什么一端封闭的管只能出现奇次谐波？
- 管口修正会怎样影响共鸣长度？
- 改变声源频率后，共鸣长度如何变化？
- 多次共鸣测量如何提高波长的测量精度？

## 八、温度对声速的影响

### 题目示例

**探究温度对空气中声速的影响。**

### 实验原理

常温下可用近似关系：

$$
v\approx331+0.6T
$$

其中 (T) 为摄氏温度。更准确的理论表达式为：

$$
v=\sqrt{\gamma\frac{RT}{M}}
$$

这里的 (T) 使用开尔文温度，因此声速近似与绝对温度的平方根成正比。

### 可视化设计

设置温度滑块，温度升高时让相同时间内的波阵面传播得更远，同时显示理论声速。将实验数据绘制成散点图，并与理论曲线比较。

### 可研究的问题

- 为什么温度升高会使声速增大？
- 摄氏温度和开尔文温度在公式中的作用有什么不同？
- 湿度和气流是否也会影响声速？
- 实验数据偏离理论曲线的原因是什么？

## 九、不同介质中的声速

### 题目示例

**比较声音在空气、水和固体中的传播速度。**

### 实验原理

流体中的声速可近似表示为：

$$
v=\sqrt{\frac{K}{\rho}}
$$

其中 (K) 为体积弹性模量，ρ 为密度。固体中的纵波速度通常与弹性模量和密度有关：

$$
v\approx\sqrt{\frac{E}{\rho}}
$$

### 可视化设计

采用分屏动画，显示相同时间内声波在空气、水和金属中的传播距离，并同步显示密度、弹性模量和声速。

### 可研究的问题

- 为什么固体中的声速通常大于液体和气体？
- 密度越大，声速是否一定越大？
- 弹性模量和密度分别如何影响声速？
- 纵波和横波在不同介质中有什么区别？

## 十、频率与波长关系的验证

### 题目示例

**验证声波的波速、频率和波长关系。**

### 实验原理

对于同一种介质：

$$
v=f\lambda
$$

改变声源频率并测量波长，可以验证：

$$
\lambda=\frac{v}{f}
$$

### 可视化设计

设置频率滑块。频率升高时，动画中单位时间内的振动次数增加、波长缩短，而声速基本保持不变。可绘制 (f-\lambda) 曲线和 (f\lambda) 数值。

### 可研究的问题

- 为什么频率变化时声速基本不变？
- 为什么频率越高，波长越短？
- 如何用线性拟合求出声速？
- 声源频率改变是否会影响测量精度？

## 十一、移动声源与多普勒效应

### 题目示例

**利用多普勒效应测量声速。**

### 实验原理

当声源相对于观察者运动时，接收到的频率会发生变化。对于观察者静止、声源以速度 (v_s) 向观察者运动的情况：

$$
f'=\frac{v}{v-v_s}f
$$

由发射频率、接收频率和声源速度可以反推声速。

### 可视化设计

显示移动声源、波阵面、观察者和接收波形。改变声源速度时，实时绘制接收频率与发射频率之差。

### 可研究的问题

- 为什么声源前方波长变短、后方波长变长？
- 声源速度接近声速时会发生什么？
- 如何区分声源运动和观察者运动造成的频移？

## 十二、基于录音波形的声速测量

### 题目示例

**利用手机录音和数字信号处理测量声速。**

### 实验原理

录制声音传播过程，利用波形中的峰值、突变点或互相关峰确定声音到达时间。若传播距离为 (d)，时间差为 Δt，则：

$$
v=\frac{d}{\Delta t}
$$

### 可视化设计

设计完整的数据处理流程：

1. 导入录音文件；
2. 显示原始波形；
3. 对信号进行滤波；
4. 自动或手动标记到达时间；
5. 计算时间差和声速；
6. 输出多次测量结果和不确定度。

### 可研究的问题

- 不同滤波方法对结果有什么影响？
- 噪声为什么会产生错误峰值？
- 采样率越高，时间测量是否一定越准确？
- 如何估计声速测量的不确定度？

## 十三、不同测量方法的比较

### 题目示例

**空气中声速的多种测量方法比较与误差分析。**

| 方法 | 主要测量量 | 主要优点 | 主要误差来源 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 回声法 | 往返时间差 | 原理简单 | 回声识别困难、人工计时误差 |
| 双麦克风法 | 到达时间差 | 易于数字化处理 | 麦克风同步和定位误差 |
| 共鸣法 | 共鸣长度 | 现象明显 | 管口修正、共鸣位置判断 |
| 驻波法 | 波节间距 | 波动图像清晰 | 波节定位误差、反射不完全 |
| 相位差法 | 相位差 | 测量精度较高 | 相位周期性造成的歧义 |
| 李萨如法 | 图形形状 | 视觉效果好 | 图形判断存在主观性 |
| 录音分析法 | 波形时间差 | 便于自动处理 | 噪声、采样率和滤波影响 |

### 可视化内容

可以绘制各方法的：

- 测量值与理论值对比图；
- 相对误差柱状图；
- 多次测量的散点图或箱线图；
- 不确定度和误差来源对比图。

# 声速测量可视化实验详细说明

## 一、文档说明

本文根据《声速测量的可视化演示题目》整理，对其中提到的各类实验逐一展开。每个实验均从实验目的、物理原理、装置与变量、操作步骤、可视化设计、数据处理、误差来源和拓展问题等方面说明，适合用于 Python、Jupyter Notebook、Streamlit 或网页交互式实验项目。

实验中的声速默认指声波在空气中的传播速度。室温下空气中的理论值通常约为 340 m/s，具体数值会受到温度、湿度、气流、频率和测量系统的影响。

## 三、实验一：回声法测量声速

### 3.1 实验目的

通过测量声音从声源传播到障碍物再返回接收端的时间，计算空气中的声速。该实验适合展示声音的反射、传播距离与时间差之间的关系。

### 3.2 实验原理

声源与反射墙之间的距离为 d。声音从声源传播到墙面，再从墙面返回接收端，总路程近似为 2d。若发声和接收回声的时间差为 Δt，则：

$$
v=\frac{2d}{\Delta t}
$$

如果发声点和接收麦克风不在同一位置，应根据实际几何路径计算总路程，而不能简单使用 2d。

### 3.3 实验装置

- 声源：扬声器、拍手声、气球爆裂声或短脉冲声；
- 接收设备：麦克风、手机或计算机声卡；
- 反射面：平整坚硬的墙面；
- 距离测量工具：卷尺或激光测距仪；
- 数据处理工具：录音软件、Python 或网页程序。

### 3.4 实验步骤

1. 测量声源到墙面的距离 d；
2. 将麦克风放在声源附近并开始录音；
3. 发出持续时间很短的声音脉冲；
4. 在录音波形中识别直接声和回声；
5. 测量两个波峰之间的时间差 Δt；
6. 根据公式计算声速；
7. 改变墙面距离，重复测量多组数据；
8. 绘制距离与时间差的关系图，通过斜率计算声速。

### 3.5 推荐的可视化

动画区域显示声源、墙面和往返传播的声波。波形区域同时绘制直接声和回声，并用两条竖直标记线表示两个到达时刻。数据区域绘制：

$$
2d-\Delta t
$$

### 3.6 主要误差

- 墙面不是理想平面，回声会展宽或分裂；
- 直接声和回声距离太近时，两个波形重叠；
- 人工读取峰值存在主观误差；
- 风会改变声音的传播时间；
- 声源和麦克风位置不完全重合；
- 墙面距离测量误差会被放大为往返距离误差。

- 能否用互相关函数自动识别回声？
- 温度改变时，回声时间是否符合理论声速变化？

## 四、实验二：双麦克风时间差法

### 4.1 实验目的

使用两个相距已知的麦克风，通过测量同一声波到达两个位置的时间差，直接计算声速。这是最适合数字化和自动化的声速测量方法之一。

### 4.2 实验原理

两个麦克风沿声波传播方向排列，相距 d。声音先到达麦克风 1，再到达麦克风 2。如果到达时间差为 Δt，则：

$$
v=\frac{d}{\Delta t}
$$

### 4.2 实验原理

两个麦克风沿声波传播方向排列，相距 d。声音先到达麦克风 1，再到达麦克风 2。如果到达时间差为 Δt，则：

$$
v=\frac{d}{\Delta t}
$$

声源不必位于两个麦克风的正前方，但应根据实际传播方向和麦克风连线方向修正有效距离：

$$
v=\frac{d\cos\theta}{\Delta t}
$$

其中 θ 是声波传播方向与麦克风连线方向的夹角。

### 4.3 实验装置

- 两个特性尽量相同的麦克风；
- 双通道声卡或具有同步采样功能的采集卡；
- 脉冲声源或连续正弦声源；
- 可调节的麦克风支架；
- 计算机和信号处理程序。

### 4.4 实验步骤

1. 将两个麦克风固定在同一直线上；
2. 用卷尺测量麦克风间距 d；
3. 将两个麦克风接入同步采集设备；
4. 发出短脉冲或稳定的周期信号；
5. 记录两个通道的波形；
6. 通过峰值、阈值或互相关函数确定时间差；
7. 计算声速并重复多次；
8. 改变 d，绘制 d-Δt 关系图并线性拟合。

### 4.5 互相关处理

设两个麦克风采集的信号分别为 x(t) 和 y(t)，互相关函数可写为：

$$
R_{xy}(\tau)=\int x(t)y(t+\tau)\,dt
$$

当 (R_{xy}(\tau)) 达到最大值时，对应的 τ 可作为时间延迟估计。离散数据中可以使用数组互相关，并将最大相关点换算为时间：

$$
\Delta t=\frac{k_{\max}}{f_s}
$$

其中 (k_{\max}) 是最大相关峰对应的采样点偏移，(f_s) 是采样频率。

## 五、实验三：示波器相位差法

### 5.1 实验目的

通过示波器双通道观察两个位置的声波信号，利用相位差或时间差测量声速，重点展示传播距离和相位变化之间的联系。

### 5.2 实验原理

两个麦克风间距为 d，声波频率为 f。若两路信号的时间差为 Δt，则：

$$
v=\frac{d}{\Delta t}
$$

由于 (T=1/f)，相位差 Δφ 与时间差的关系为：
title: 声速测量各实验详细说明

source: 声速测量各实验详细说明.md
text:
离和相位变化之间的联系。

### 5.2 实验原理

两个麦克风间距为 d，声波频率为 f。若两路信号的时间差为 Δt，则：

$$
v=\frac{d}{\Delta t}
$$

由于 (T=1/f)，相位差 Δφ 与时间差的关系为：

$$
\frac{\Delta t}{T}=\frac{\Delta\varphi}{2\pi}
$$

因此：

$$
v=\frac{2\pi f d}{\Delta\varphi}
$$

### 5.3 实验步骤

1. 将两个麦克风接入示波器 CH1 和 CH2；
2. 选择稳定的正弦声源；
3. 调整触发和垂直灵敏度，使两个波形清晰显示；
4. 测量一个周期 T 和两路信号的水平位移 Δt；
5. 计算相位差；
6. 根据麦克风间距和频率计算声速；
7. 改变麦克风距离，观察相位差的周期性变化。

### 5.4 动态模型

可用以下模型生成两路波形：

$$
y_1=A\sin(2\pi ft)
$$

$$
y_2=A\sin(2\pi ft-\Delta\varphi)
$$

可视化中拖动 d 时，应同步改变 Δφ。距离每增加一个波长，图形会恢复为近似相同的相位关系。

### 5.5 相位多值性问题

实际相位差只能在一个周期内测量，而传播距离可能包含多个完整波长：

$$
d=n\lambda+\Delta d
$$

因此仅测量一次相位差不能确定整数 n。解决方法包括：

- 连续改变麦克风距离，记录相位重复出现的位置；
- 选择较低频率，使波长变长；
- 同时使用时间差法获得粗略距离，再用相位法精确修正；
- 使用多个频率进行相位解包裹。

### 5.6 主要误差

## 六、实验四：利用李萨如图形测量声速

### 6.1 实验目的

将两个同频声波信号分别接入示波器 X、Y 输入，通过李萨如图形判断相位差，进而测量声速。该实验具有很强的视觉效果，适合互动式演示。

### 6.2 实验原理

两路信号可表示为：

$$
x=A\sin(\omega t)
$$

$$
y=B\sin(\omega t+\varphi)
$$

当频率相同，图形通常为直线、椭圆或圆：

- φ = 0：正向直线；
- φ = π：反向直线；
- φ = π/2 且 A = B：圆；
- 其他相位差：椭圆。

通过图形反推出相位差，再使用：

$$
v=\frac{2\pi f d}{\Delta\varphi}
$$

也可以改变 d，测量相位重复周期，得到波长后使用 (v=f\lambda)。

## 七、实验五：空气柱共鸣法

### 7.1 实验目的

利用空气柱在特定长度下产生共鸣的现象测量波长，再由 (v=f\lambda) 求声速。这是最适合展示共鸣峰、波节和波腹的实验之一。

### 7.2 实验原理

对于一端封闭、一端开口的管，开口端近似为位移波腹，封闭端近似为位移波节。前两个共鸣长度可近似写为：

$$
L_1=\frac{\lambda}{4},\qquad L_2=\frac{3\lambda}{4}
$$

相邻共鸣长度之差为：

$$
L_2-L_1=\frac{\lambda}{2}
$$

于是：

$$
v=2f(L_2-L_1)
$$

### 7.3 实验装置

- 共鸣管或可调长度的空气柱；
- 扬声器或音叉；
- 麦克风或声级计；
- 活塞、水面或可移动挡板；
- 管长和管径测量工具。

### 7.3 实验装置

- 共鸣管或可调长度的空气柱；
- 扬声器或音叉；
- 麦克风或声级计；
- 活塞、水面或可移动挡板；
- 管长和管径测量工具。

### 7.4 实验步骤

1. 设定声源频率 f；
2. 缓慢改变空气柱长度；
3. 记录声强或麦克风振幅达到峰值的位置；
4. 找到相邻两个共鸣长度；
5. 计算波长和声速；
6. 对多个共鸣峰进行线性拟合，提高精度。

### 7.5 可视化设计

用质点动画表示管内空气振动，在共鸣位置增大振幅。在下方绘制振幅与管长的关系 (A(L))，用峰值标记共鸣位置，并显示波节和波腹。

### 7.6 管口修正

实际空气柱的声学长度通常略大于几何长度，可使用修正长度：

$$
L_{\mathrm{eff}}=L+\delta L
$$

管口修正与管半径 r 有关。若忽略该修正，短管或粗管实验中的系统误差会较明显。

### 7.7 主要误差

- 共鸣峰不够尖锐，峰值位置难以确定；
- 管口修正未考虑；
- 声源频率不稳定；
- 环境噪声影响声强测量；
- 空气柱长度读取误差。

## 八、实验六：驻波法测量声速

### 8.1 实验目的

观察入射波与反射波叠加形成驻波的过程，测量相邻波节或波腹之间的距离，从而计算声速。

### 8.2 实验原理

一列向右传播的波和一列向左传播的波叠加：

$$
y_1=A\sin(kx-\omega t)
$$

$$
y_2=A\sin(kx+\omega t)
$$

相加得到：

$$
y=2A\sin(kx)\cos(\omega t)
$$

相邻波节之间的距离为 λ/2。若测得相邻波节间距 d，则：

$$
v=2fd
$$

### 8.3 实验步骤

1. 在管中设置稳定声源和反射端；
2. 调节频率或管长，使反射波与入射波形成明显驻波；
3. 用麦克风、探针或模拟质点振幅确定波节位置；
4. 测量多个连续波节的位置；
5. 对波节编号与位置进行线性拟合；
6. 由斜率得到半波长，再计算声速。

### 8.4 可视化设计

分别用不同颜色显示入射波、反射波和合成驻波。用亮度表示振幅，波节处亮度最弱，波腹处亮度最强。可提供暂停、单步播放和改变频率功能。

### 8.5 主要误差

- 反射不完全导致驻波不理想；
- 波节位置不是绝对静止的零振幅点；
- 管壁吸声和声源阻抗影响振幅；
- 多个波节距离测量不准。

### 8.6 拓展问题

- 如何从驻波动画中区分行波和驻波？
- 为什么测量多个波节可以减小随机误差？
- 一端开口和两端开口的边界条件有什么不同？

### 9.2 实验原理

常温范围内，空气中声速可近似表示为：

$$
v\approx331+0.6T_c

：温度对声速的影响

### 9.1 实验目的

研究空气温度变化对声速的影响，验证理论模型，并理解温度改变的微观原因。

### 9.2 实验原理

常温范围内，空气中声速可近似表示为：

$$
v\approx331+0.6T_c
$$

其中 (T_c) 为摄氏温度。理想气体模型给出：

$$
v=\sqrt{\gamma\frac{RT_K}{M}}
$$

其中 (T_K) 必须使用开尔文温度。

### 9.3 实验设计

可使用同一套双麦克风或回声装置，在不同温度下重复测量声速。温度可以通过自然环境变化、恒温箱或加热/冷却管道实现。

每次测量记录：温度、距离、时间差、声速和环境湿度。尽量保持声源频率、麦克风间距和测量路径不变。

### 9.4 可视化设计

- 温度滑块控制声波传播速度；
- 相同时间内显示不同温度下的传播距离；
- 绘制 (v-T_c) 散点图和理论拟合直线；
- 同时显示摄氏温度和开尔文温度，避免单位混淆。

### 9.5 主要误差

- 温度传感器与声波实际传播区域温度不一致；
- 管道或房间内存在温度梯度；
- 湿度和气流未控制；
- 温度变化引起设备响应变化；
- 直接用摄氏温度代入平方根公式。

### 9.6 拓展问题

- 湿度升高时声速为什么可能发生变化？
- 气流方向与声波传播方向相同时，测得的传播速度如何变化？
- 能否利用声速测量反推出未知温度？

比较空气、水和固体中的声速，理解声速与介质弹性和密度之间的关系。

### 10.2 实验原理

流体中的声速可近似表示为：

$$
v=\sqrt{\frac{K}{\rho}}
$$

八：不同介质中的声速

### 10.1 实验目的

比较空气、水和固体中的声速，理解声速与介质弹性和密度之间的关系。

### 10.2 实验原理

流体中的声速可近似表示为：

$$
v=\sqrt{\frac{K}{\rho}}
$$

其中 K 是体积弹性模量，ρ 是密度。固体纵波速度常与杨氏模量 E 和密度有关：

$$
v\approx\sqrt{\frac{E}{\rho}}
$$

声速不由密度单独决定，而由介质抵抗压缩或形变的能力与惯性共同决定。

### 10.3 实验方案

- 空气：双麦克风时间差法或回声法；
- 水：水槽、换能器和相位比较法；
- 固体：金属棒或木棒两端布置压电换能器，测量超声脉冲飞行时间。

### 10.4 可视化设计

采用分屏动画，三个介质在同一时间轴上显示声波传播距离。旁边显示密度、弹性模量和声速。可以将相同能量的波用质点间距和恢复力大小表示。

### 10.5 主要误差

- 不同介质的换能器耦合条件不同；
- 水槽边界产生多次反射；
- 固体材料内部存在缺陷或不均匀性；
- 传播模式可能混入横波、表面波或弯曲波；
- 密度和弹性参数使用了不适合当前温度的数值。

### 10.6 拓展问题

- 为什么固体中声速通常高于液体和气体？
- 密度增大但弹性模量也增大时，声速如何判断？
- 如何区分纵波和横波的传播速度？

## 十一、实验九：频率与波长关系的验证

### 11.1 实验目的

验证波速、频率和波长之间的基本关系：

$$
v=f\lambda
$$

并说明在同一均匀介质中改变频率通常不会直接改变波速。

### 11.2 实验步骤

1. 选择多个声源频率；
2. 对每个频率测量相邻共鸣长度或驻波波节间距；
3. 计算相应波长；
4. 绘制频率-波长关系图；
5. 绘制 (f\lambda) 或波速-频率关系图；
6. 对结果进行线性或非线性拟合。

### 11.3 可视化设计

用频率滑块改变声波动画。频率升高时，波峰在单位时间内出现得更密集，波长缩短，但传播速度保持近似恒定。

可以同时显示：

- 时域波形；
- 空间波形；
- 当前频率和波长；
- (f\lambda) 的计算值；
- 理论值与测量值差异。

### 11.4 主要误差

- 波长测量误差；
- 声源频率显示值与实际频率有差异；
- 介质温度或边界条件发生变化；
- 频率过高时采样和空间分辨率不足。

### 11.5 拓展问题

- 在色散介质中，为什么不同频率的波速可能不同？
- 如何区分相速度和群速度？
- 若保持声速不变，频率加倍后波长如何变化？

## 十二、实验十：移动声源与多普勒效应

### 12.1 实验目的

通过观察移动声源造成的接收频率变化，研究波阵面压缩和拉伸，并尝试反推出声速。

### 12.2 实验原理

观察者静止、声源以速度 (v_s) 向观察者运动时：

$$
f'=\frac{v}{v-v_s}f
$$

若声源远离观察者，则：

$$
f'=\frac{v}{v+v_s}f
$$

其中 f 是发射频率，f' 是接收频率，v 是介质中的声速。

### 12.3 实验方案

- 使用小车或电动滑轨带动扬声器；
- 使用固定麦克风记录接收信号；
- 同时测量声源速度；
- 通过频谱峰值或零交叉法测量接收频率；
- 改变声源运动方向和速度，重复实验。

### 12.4 可视化设计

动画显示移动声源和波阵面。声源前方波阵面变密，后方变疏；图表显示声源速度与接收频率的关系，并对理论曲线和实验点进行比较。

### 12.5 主要误差

- 声源速度不恒定；
- 麦克风接收到反射声；
- 频率估计窗口太短；
- 声源与观察者不在同一直线上；
- 风速叠加改变有效传播速度。

### 12.6 拓展问题

- 声源运动和观察者运动的公式有什么区别？
- 当声源速度接近声速时，波阵面会怎样变化？
- 能否用多普勒频移测量移动物体速度？

## 十三、实验十一：基于录音波形的声速测量

### 13.1 实验目的

把声速测量转化为完整的数字信号处理流程，学习录音、滤波、峰值检测、互相关和不确定度分析。

### 13.2 实验原理

若已知传播距离 d，通过录音波形得到时间差 Δt，则：

$$
v=\frac{d}{\Delta t}
$$

当波形含有噪声时，可以先进行带通滤波或使用互相关函数确定延迟。

### 13.3 标准处理流程

### 13.2 实验原理

若已知传播距离 d，通过录音波形得到时间差 Δt，则：

$$
v=\frac{d}{\Delta t}
$$

当波形含有噪声时，可以先进行带通滤波或使用互相关函数确定延迟。

### 13.3 标准处理流程

1. 读取 WAV 或其他格式的录音；
2. 检查采样率、声道数和采样位数；
3. 将双声道信号分离；
4. 去除直流分量并进行归一化；
5. 根据声源频率设计滤波器；
6. 使用峰值、阈值或互相关确定到达时刻；
7. 根据采样点差计算 Δt；
8. 计算声速并输出置信区间。

### 13.4 可视化设计

建议按处理流程分层显示：原始波形、滤波波形、检测到达点、互相关曲线、频谱和最终结果。每一步都提供“处理前/处理后”切换，便于观察算法对信号的影响。

### 13.5 主要误差

- 录音设备自动增益改变波形振幅；
- 左右声道存在硬件延迟；
- 噪声造成错误峰值；
- 采样率限制时间分辨率；
- 滤波器相位响应造成额外延迟；
- 文件中含有压缩或重采样造成的时间误差。

### 13.6 拓展问题

- 如何比较峰值检测和互相关检测的稳定性？
- 如何利用亚采样插值提高延迟估计精度？
- 如何由多次测量计算标准差和合成不确定度？

text:
四、实验十二：不同测量方法的比较与误差分析

### 14.1 实验目的

在相同理论声速和相同环境条件下，比较回声法、双麦克风法、共鸣法、驻波法、相位差法、李萨如法和录音分析法的精度、复杂度与适用场景。

### 14.2 建议的比较指标

| 指标 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 准确度 | 测量平均值接近理论值的程度 |
| 精密度 | 多次测量结果的离散程度 |
| 操作难度 | 所需设备和实验步骤复杂程度 |
| 自动化程度 | 是否可以由程序自动识别和计算 |
| 可视化效果 | 是否能直观展示声波现象 |
| 主要误差 | 对结果影响最大的误差来源 |
| 适用范围 | 适合课堂、竞赛或科研的场景 |

### 14.3 实验流程

1. 设定统一的温度、湿度和声源条件；
2. 对每种方法进行相同次数的重复测量；
3. 记录每次测量的原始数据，而不只保存最终声速；
4. 计算平均值、标准差、绝对误差和相对误差；
5. 绘制箱线图、误差柱状图和理论值对比图；
6. 对不同方法的设备成本、操作时间和可视化程度进行评分。

### 14.4 推荐图表

- 各方法声速测量值与理论值的散点图；
- 各方法相对误差的柱状图；
- 多次测量结果的箱线图；
- 测量时间与误差的关系图；
- “准确度—操作复杂度”二维散点图。

### 14.5 结论表达

比较实验不能只说某一种方法“最好”。应根据任务目标进行评价：

- 入门教学通常选择回声法或空气柱共鸣法；
- 数字信号处理适合双麦克风法和录音波形法；
- 相位与波动现象适合示波器相位差法和李萨如法；
- 复杂声场和高精度实验需要驻波、超声或多传感器方案。

## 十五、综合虚拟实验室的实现建议

### 15.1 模块结构

建议将虚拟实验室设计为以下页面或标签页：

1. 回声与时间差；
2. 双麦克风与互相关；
3. 相位差与李萨如图形；
4. 空气柱共鸣与驻波；
5. 温度和介质参数；
6. 录音导入与数字处理；
7. 多方法误差比较。

### 15.2 统一交互控件

- 距离滑块；
- 频率输入框；
- 温度滑块；
- 噪声强度滑块；
- 播放、暂停和单步按钮；
- 理想模型/实验数据切换；
- 导出数据和导出图像按钮。

### 15.3 运行状态提示

当程序正在计算互相关、滤波、拟合或生成动画时，应显示“正在计算……”或进度条，并暂时禁用重复提交按钮。计算完成后显示“计算完成”，发生异常时显示具体错误原因。

### 15.4 结果输出

每个实验至少输出：

- 实验参数；
- 原始测量数据；
- 理论公式；
- 计算结果；
- 不确定度；
- 理论值比较；
- 误差分析；
- 可下载的图像或 CSV 数据。

## 十六、项目实施优先级

### 第一阶段：基础演示

先实现回声法、空气柱共鸣法和驻波法，重点完成传播动画、共鸣峰和波节波腹显示。

### 第二阶段：数字测量

加入双麦克风时间差法、录音波形分析和互相关算法，实现真实数据导入。

### 第三阶段：相位可视化

加入示波器相位差法和李萨如图形法，处理相位周期性和图形拟合问题。

### 第四阶段：综合分析

加入温度、介质、频率和多普勒效应模块，并制作多种方法的误差比较页面。
